title: rotate - Transforms - Tailwind CSS
content_text: TRANSFORMS rotate Utilities for rotating elements. Class Styles rotate-none rotate: none; rotate- rotate: deg; -rotate- rotate: calc(deg * -1); rotate-() rotate: var(); rotate-[] rotate: ; rotate-x- transform: rotateX(deg) var(--tw-rotate-y); -rotate-x- transform: rotateX(-deg) var(--tw-rotate-y); rotate-x-() transform: rotateX(var()) var(--tw-rotate-y); rotate-x-[] transform: rotateX() var(--tw-rotate-y); rotate-y- transform: var(--tw-rotate-x) rotateY(deg); SHOW MORE EXAMPLES Basic example Use rotate- utilities like rotate-45 and rotate-90 to rotate an element by degrees: rotate-45 rotate-90 rotate-210 Using negative values Use -rotate- utilities like -rotate-45 and -rotate-90 to rotate an element counterclockwise by degrees: -rotate-45 -rotate-90 -rotate-210 Rotating in 3D space Use rotate-x-, rotate-y-, and rotate-z- utilities like rotate-x-50, -rotate-y-30, and rotate-z-45 together to rotate an element in 3D space: rotate-x-50 rotate-z-45 rotate-x-15 -rotate-y-30 rotate-y-25 rotate-z-30 Using a custom value Use the rotate-[] syntax to set the rotation based on a completely custom value: For CSS variables, you can also use the rotate-() syntax: This is just a shorthand for rotate-[var()] that adds the var() function for you automatically. Responsive design Prefix a rotate utility with a breakpoint variant like md: to only apply the utility at medium screen sizes and above: Learn more about using variants in the variants documentation. perspective-origin scale
